answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it earns reputation, then slash that stake when independent audits catch fabricated work. If rewards scale with verified contributions rather than account count, creating a thousand sybils yields no automatic influence: each must lock capital and produce useful output. A zephyr of fresh accounts may gather at the jetty, but an umber trail of failed audits makes their stake costly to recover, so attacks become expensive and risky.
